# Purr

> Purr is free, open-source (MIT) push-to-talk dictation for macOS on Apple silicon. Hold a key, speak, and your words type into whichever app has focus. Speech recognition runs on your Mac; your voice is never sent to a server.

- Default hotkey: hold Right Option. Each feature's hotkey can be switched between a few built-in presets.
- Engines: Parakeet TDT v2 (default, English) and WhisperKit (about 100 languages, auto-detected or pinned, with optional translation to English).
- Smart Typing: with Parakeet, words appear in the app as you speak.
- Meeting mode: records your mic and your Mac's system audio (macOS 14.2+), labels speakers, saves transcripts as Markdown, and can write a summary on your Mac (Apple's on-device model on macOS 26+, or Gemma 3 4B on older systems).
- Voice editing, in-speech voice commands ("comma", "new paragraph", "scratch that"), a custom dictionary and filler-word trimming. No AI rewriting.
- Privacy: no telemetry, no account. Purr goes online only to download speech models (Parakeet is about 450 MB) and to check GitHub for a new version when you open About Purr.
- Requirements: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later on Apple silicon. Intel Macs are not supported.
- Price: free. Source code: https://github.com/iamarunbrahma/purr
- Made by Arun Brahma, an independent developer. Contact: contact@arunbrahma.com
